newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs higher as strong yen eases rate fears.
newsitem.headline: JGBs higher as strong yen eases rate fears.

text.p: Key September 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) futures rose in early trade on Wednesday as concerns about the possibility of higher Japanese interest rates eased on the yen's strength against the dollar.
"There was a persisting view in the market that it will be difficult for the Bank of Japan to raise interest rates so long as the strong yen curbs exports," said a dealer at a bank's securities unit.
The yen retained its overnight firmness after the release of Japan's current account data for April, which showed a jump of 92.7 percent to 1.09 trillion yen.
The September stood up 0.21 at 123.35 at 0056 GMT after opening at 123.29.

Activity in cash bonds was slow compared with futures, where buy orders came in in large lots from the opening, the dealer said. The yield of key 182nd 10-year JGB stood down 0.015 at 2.465 percent after opening at 2.475 percent.
Traders said sentiment had improved since Japan released weaker-than-expected April machinery orders data on Tuesday.
But JGBs were capped on the upside since 300 billion to 400 billion yen worth of corporate straight bonds are due to be launched this week and next, they said.
